moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
learningObjectives: Explain Blueprint’s independent SaaS design workflow and editable proposals
Review application context, workflows, data and Personas before export
Distinguish a PDF summary from the technical .blueprint import file
Configure build, inherit, reuse and skip choices in the import wizard
Review branch placement and complete post-import implementation checks

elements.description: Blueprint supports collaborative workflow design using industry templates or generative AI. It proposes a starting point that teams review against their requirements.

elements.text: Think of Blueprint as a draft building plan: align the team on structure, then refine and implement it. A proposal is not proof of production readiness or a guaranteed delivery time.

elements.description: Blueprint is SaaS, independent of a Pega Platform development instance and Operator login. SaaS sign-in and collaboration access still apply; knowing a URL does not imply unrestricted access. Its interface evolves continually.
Blueprint accelerates initial design; App Studio and Dev Studio support implementation and review after import. Templates are starting points, not substitutes for configuration and testing.

elements.caption: Design and implementation are separate steps. Access Roles are the branch-placement exception, not an asset type excluded from creation.

elements.description: Provide industry, sub-industry, department, purpose and a functional description. Use Other for an unlisted industry. Choose a template or GenAI, supply organization/language details and upload relevant supporting assets.

Review Case Types with stakeholders. Edit Primary/Alternate Stages, Processes and Steps; use Notes for routing, SLA and conditions. Preview my app supports design review. Check fields, types, descriptions, primary fields, single/multiple records and user-input/calculated sources.

Templates offer an industry starting point. Review Personas, access needs, Channels and release effort, then check the summary for workflow, data and integration completeness. Export PDF for reference or .blueprint for import; revision history and dashboard support ongoing changes. A live-demo option can provision an instance and import the design.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Importing a Pega Blueprint into Pega Platform

elements.description: In App Studio, create an application with Build from a Blueprint and upload the technical file. Verify its details and intended built-on stack. Using an existing application through the New Application wizard requires saving that application as a template.

The authorized implementation team imports and reviews the application. Assign technical responsibility within the project; the source does not impose an LSA-only permission or a separate import ceremony.

For the documented new-application workflow, created assets except Access Roles go into a Branch. This is about placement, not whether Access Roles are created. Base Rulesets are locked; use the provided password for appropriate merges and store it securely.
Pega GenAI PremBridge is NOT required to import Pega Blueprints into a new or existing application.

elements.description: For Case Types choose build, inherit or skip. For data objects choose build, inherit, reuse or skip: inheritance creates a new object; reuse links to the built-on object without its own new class. Build or skip Personas. Check class layers and Case/data classes before Submit, then inspect the result and add users with Personas.

Check existing-app overlap before extending it. After import, prepare developer configuration and merges, refine Decision shapes, Flow Actions and locking, and validate database mappings, Data Pages and properties. Test alternate paths, approvals, automation and child Cases.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Using Blueprint for an Industry App (Customer Service for Insurance)

elements.description: The insurance example starts with a Customer Service template and adds a golf-cart Case. It inherits existing service Case Types and builds the new Case Type; infrastructure Cases also appear. A weather Step and field are separate design changes. After import, change the field to Picklist and add it to a View. Configure data, integrations, Channels and user groups, then simulate an interaction and review wrap-up/recent Cases. The example’s creation time is not a project guarantee.

examPitfalls.title: Independent SaaS is not unrestricted access
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not confuse independence from a Platform instance/Operator login with absence of SaaS sign-in or collaboration permissions.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the separate Blueprint service with appropriate access.

examPitfalls.title: Blueprint augments, not replaces, App Studio
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks whether Blueprint replaces App Studio. Candidates say yes because Blueprint generates the same artifacts. Blueprint is a GenAI accelerator that generates a starting point — all generated content is then configured and refined inside App Studio.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Blueprint augments existing tools by accelerating design; you still build/refine in App Studio.

examPitfalls.title: What Blueprint proposes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask what a Blueprint import creates. Candidates list only Case Types. Blueprint proposes Case Types, fields, stages, and processes — a fuller skeleton than just the Case Type shell.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Blueprint drafts the app skeleton (workflow + data + personas), not infrastructure or production integrations.

examPitfalls.title: Import responsibility versus permissions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Project roles do not establish universal import permissions. Assign an authorized developer/team to import and review the generated assets.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Validate target environment access and project responsibilities.

examPitfalls.title: Import creates assets in a Branch EXCEPT Access Roles
examPitfalls.trapDescription: In the documented new-application import, Access Roles are outside the Branch. This does not mean that Access Roles are not created.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If asked which asset is NOT created in the Branch on import, the answer is Access Roles.

examPitfalls.title: PremBridge is not required to import
examPitfalls.trapDescription: PremBridge is not required for Blueprint import. This does not eliminate the target environment’s access and configuration requirements.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Pega GenAI PremBridge is NOT required to import a Blueprint into a new or existing application.

examPitfalls.title: Existing application reuse needs review
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Blueprint can extend an existing application, but check overlaps. To use an existing application through the New Application wizard, save it as a template.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review the built-on stack and inheritance/reuse choices.

examPitfalls.title: Best-practice templates value
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Industry templates help start a design. They do not guarantee zero technical debt, guardrail compliance or production readiness.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Refine the template and validate implementation requirements.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A business team without access to a Pega Platform development instance wants to design an application before development begins. What makes Blueprint suitable?

options.text: It is independent SaaS; a Platform development instance or Operator login is not required to begin design
It runs inside Dev Studio, but stakeholders can be granted temporary guest access without a full Pega license
It requires every participant to have an LSA-level license so the designs are authoritative and can be imported
It can only be used after the Pega Platform environment has been provisioned, since it reads existing Case Type metadata

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the SaaS design service from a Platform environment.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint operates independently of a Pega Platform instance. Business stakeholders can collaborate on an application proposal before implementation, rather than receiving temporary access to Dev Studio.

optionExplanations.A: Independent SaaS design does not require an existing Platform application.
optionExplanations.B: The independent service is not a guest mode inside Dev Studio.
optionExplanations.C: The curriculum does not require every collaborator to hold an LSA license.
optionExplanations.D: Provisioning a Platform environment is not required to begin the design proposal.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA describes a new 'Claims Management' application to Pega Blueprint in plain business language. What does Blueprint propose in response?

options.text: Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas — the full application design skeleton
Server hardware specifications, network topology, and database schema — the infrastructure design for the application
A list of Rulesets and their version numbers — the packaging structure for the application's deployable artifacts
Access Roles and Operator IDs — the security and user configuration for all roles in the Claims Management system

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint drafts the 'what' of the application — its Case Types, data, and user roles.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint proposes the application design: Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas — the structural skeleton you then refine and import. It generates structure, not a production-ready application.

optionExplanations.A: The proposal captures the workflow, business data and intended user groups.
optionExplanations.B: A business application proposal does not provision production infrastructure.
optionExplanations.C: Release-package versions are not the application design skeleton requested.
optionExplanations.D: Personas model business needs; the proposal is not a completed identity setup.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A stakeholder says, 'Now that we have Blueprint, we don't need App Studio anymore.' How should the SA respond?

options.text: Blueprint augments App Studio and other Pega tools by accelerating the initial design phase — the team still builds and refines in App Studio
The stakeholder is correct — Blueprint fully replaces App Studio for all Case Type configuration and application authoring
Blueprint replaces App Studio for initial design but is used alongside Dev Studio for implementation
Blueprint and App Studio cannot be used on the same project — teams must choose one tool for the full lifecycle

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint's design philosophy is 'augment, not replace' existing developer work.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint accelerates the pre-build design phase; after import, the team uses App Studio (and Dev Studio) to configure, refine, and build. Blueprint starts the project — App Studio finishes it.

optionExplanations.A: Blueprint complements the tools that configure the actual application.
optionExplanations.B: Generating a proposal does not replace App Studio configuration.
optionExplanations.C: It is not an exclusive replacement for App Studio's design role.
optionExplanations.D: Teams can use Blueprint and App Studio within the same project.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The project assigns its LSA responsibility for importing and configuring the reviewed Blueprint. Which team member performs that technical work in this scenario?

options.text: The Lead System Architect (LSA), as the assigned implementation owner
The Product Owner — approves the Blueprint import as a business gate before any technical work begins
The Scrum Master — facilitates the import ceremony and ensures all team members have reviewed the Blueprint before it proceeds
The end customer — reviews and approves the Blueprint export file before the LSA is authorized to import it

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the explicitly assigned responsibility, not an assumed permission restriction.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The scenario assigns the technical responsibility to the LSA. This project allocation is not a universal LSA-only import permission.

optionExplanations.A: The LSA is explicitly assigned technical responsibility in this scenario.
optionExplanations.B: Business approval does not itself execute the technical import.
optionExplanations.C: Facilitating teamwork is different from performing the technical import.
optionExplanations.D: The scenario assigns implementation to the LSA, not the end customer.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An LSA uses the documented new-application Blueprint import. Which created asset type is the exception to placement inside the Branch?

options.text: Access Roles — they are not created inside the Branch on import; all other Blueprint-generated assets (Case Types, Data Objects, Personas) are placed in the Branch
Case Types — they are created at the application level, not in the Branch, to ensure they are immediately available to all environments
Data objects — they are created directly in the production Ruleset because they represent the system of record structure
Personas — they require Admin Studio authorization before being placed in the Branch, so they are held in a staging area

practiceQuiz.hint: Which asset type is security-related and therefore excluded from the Branch?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Access Roles are outside the Branch in this workflow. The exception concerns placement, not exclusion from application creation.

optionExplanations.A: Access Roles are the documented exception to branch placement.
optionExplanations.B: Case Types are among the assets placed in the branch.
optionExplanations.C: The import does not directly create production database records this way.
optionExplanations.D: The stated Admin Studio staging requirement is not the import behavior.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA insists the team must install 'Pega GenAI PremBridge' and have an active Pega environment before they can even start generating a Blueprint proposal for a new application. Is the BA correct, and why?

options.text: No — Blueprint is a standalone SaaS tool at pega.com/blueprint; no Pega environment or PremBridge installation is needed to generate or collaborate on a Blueprint
Yes — PremBridge provides the GenAI gateway that Blueprint relies on; without it, natural-language processing during generation is unavailable
Partially — you don't need PremBridge, but you DO need an active Pega Infinity '23+ environment running before Blueprint generation can begin
Yes — Blueprint requires a Pega environment so it can validate proposed Case Types against existing rule names in the system

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint is accessed at pega.com/blueprint — no Pega installation needed.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint proposal generation is separate SaaS design. A Platform environment is not needed to begin the proposal, and PremBridge is not an import prerequisite.

optionExplanations.A: Proposal generation is independent of a Platform environment.
optionExplanations.B: PremBridge is not the stated prerequisite for the SaaS design activity.
optionExplanations.C: An existing Infinity environment is not required to begin a proposal.
optionExplanations.D: A Platform environment is not required for the initial design activity.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A sales team needs a working prototype of a 'Trade Finance' application for a client demo in two days. An LSA decides to use Blueprint. What is the primary value of importing the Blueprint into Pega Platform for this scenario?

options.text: Blueprint import accelerates creation of an editable application skeleton for the team to demonstrate, configure and test
Blueprint import permanently locks the application to the Blueprint design, ensuring the demo exactly matches the agreed specifications
Blueprint import deletes any existing Case Types in the target application and replaces them with the Blueprint's design
Blueprint import disables App Studio to prevent unauthorized edits to the generated application during the demo period

practiceQuiz.hint: From a business-terms description to a working demo in minutes — what does Blueprint import enable?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Import accelerates the initial application skeleton. It remains editable and needs configuration and testing; a delivery time is not guaranteed.

optionExplanations.A: Import supplies a starting application for demonstration and further configuration.
optionExplanations.B: The imported design remains available for refinement.
optionExplanations.C: Import is not described as deleting every existing Case Type.
optionExplanations.D: App Studio remains part of application configuration after import.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA and SA collaborate in Pega Blueprint before any development begins. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Blueprint is generated and modified?

options.text: You describe the application in business terms (natural language) and Blueprint proposes an initial Case Types, Data Models, and Personas design
You can refine the Blueprint proposal — editing Stages, Steps, fields, data objects, and Personas — before importing into Pega Platform
Once a Blueprint is generated it is locked and cannot be edited; all refinements must happen after import in App Studio
Blueprint generation requires the SA to write a JSON schema file describing the Case Types before the AI can propose a design

practiceQuiz.hint: Natural language in → proposal out → refine → then import. Which two steps fit?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Describe the intended application, review the proposed Case Types, Data Models and Personas, and refine the proposal before import. Blueprint is a collaborative starting point rather than an immutable specification.

optionExplanations.A: A business description can guide a proposed application model.
optionExplanations.B: The team can refine the proposal before importing it.
optionExplanations.C: Proposal edits are not limited to post-import configuration.
optionExplanations.D: Writing a JSON schema is not the stated generation prerequisite.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An insurance company wants to build a 'Claims Adjudication' application using industry-accepted best practices without starting from scratch. How does Blueprint support this?

options.text: Blueprint provides industry best-practice templates that encode Pega's accumulated expertise — the team selects and refines the template for their specific needs
Blueprint forbids any customization of the generated design to ensure the application adheres strictly to the industry template
Blueprint's templates only work for generic, non-industry applications; industry-specific apps must be designed from scratch
Blueprint generates a fully configured, production-ready application from the template that requires no further refinement by the SA

practiceQuiz.hint: Industry templates give the team a best-practice starting point — then what?
practiceQuiz.rationale: An industry template supplies a starting design that the team adapts to its requirements. It is neither immutable nor automatically production-ready.

optionExplanations.A: An industry starting point can be adapted to the client's needs.
optionExplanations.B: A template does not prohibit refining its generated design.
optionExplanations.C: Industry-focused starting points are part of the stated capability.
optionExplanations.D: A starting application still requires configuration, testing and review.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Traditional Pega application design through workshops and requirements documentation took weeks to months before development could begin. Why did Pega create Blueprint?

options.text: Blueprint's GenAI-infused design approach helps teams align on an optimized solution faster and gets them into development in days instead of weeks
Blueprint was created to remove any need for business stakeholder input — the AI generates the design independently without collaboration
Blueprint was created to replace the Case Life Cycle concept with a new event-driven architecture
Blueprint was created to store production data and reduce database costs by pre-generating data objects

practiceQuiz.hint: The driver was speed-to-development and stakeholder alignment — Blueprint shortens the design phase dramatically.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint aims to accelerate design alignment using templates and GenAI. This is an intended benefit, not a guaranteed reduction to a particular number of days.

optionExplanations.A: Faster design alignment can shorten the path into implementation.
optionExplanations.B: Stakeholder collaboration remains part of the design workflow.
optionExplanations.C: Blueprint does not replace Case Lifecycle modeling.
optionExplanations.D: The design tool is not a production-data storage service.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After import, the project assigns its LSA technical implementation from the reviewed backlog and BA requirements. Who leads that configuration work in this scenario?

options.text: The Lead System Architect (LSA), as the assigned technical implementation lead
The UX Designer — translates the user stories into wireframes that are then manually configured by a separate development team
The Quality Analyst (QA) — creates test cases from the user stories but does not directly configure the application
The Solutions Consultant — demos the imported Blueprint to the client and configures requirements based on client feedback during the demo

practiceQuiz.hint: Read the project responsibility stated in the scenario.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The scenario designates the LSA as technical lead. Blueprint supplies a starting point; the implementation team still configures and validates requirements.

optionExplanations.A: The scenario explicitly assigns this configuration responsibility to the LSA.
optionExplanations.B: Wireframing is not the configuration responsibility asked in this workflow.
optionExplanations.C: Testing stories is different from implementing those requirements.
optionExplanations.D: The scenario assigns implementation leadership to the LSA, not a demo presenter.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where does a team begin collaborative Blueprint design without first provisioning a Pega Platform development instance?

options.text: At pega.com/blueprint, the separate SaaS service, with its appropriate sign-in and collaboration access
Open Admin Studio and navigate to the Blueprint tab — Blueprint is built into the Pega administration console and requires admin credentials
Use Prediction Studio's Blueprint module — it is co-located with AI model management because Blueprint uses the same GenAI infrastructure
Open App Studio → New Application → Blueprint mode — Blueprint is a guided wizard launched from within an existing Pega application

practiceQuiz.hint: The design service is separate from the Platform Studios.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Start at the separate Blueprint service. Independence from a Platform instance does not imply unrestricted or anonymous SaaS access.

optionExplanations.A: The independent Blueprint service is the starting point described.
optionExplanations.B: The initial design tool is not an Admin Studio tab.
optionExplanations.C: Prediction Studio is not where the standalone service is launched.
optionExplanations.D: An existing Platform application is not a prerequisite for starting design.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An LSA uses the documented new-application Build from a Blueprint workflow. Which TWO statements are correct?

options.text: Using an existing application as the built-on template through this wizard requires saving that application as a template
Created assets except Access Roles go into a Branch; this is a placement exception
Import always overwrites and deletes all existing Case Types in the target application
Only the Business Analyst, as the Blueprint author, can perform the import

practiceQuiz.hint: Review the built-on template requirement and the branch-placement exception.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The wizard supports a saved existing-app template as the built-on application. In this new-application workflow, Access Roles are the exception to branch placement.

optionExplanations.A: The cited wizard requires the existing application to be saved as a template.
optionExplanations.B: Access Roles are the exception to the documented branch placement.
optionExplanations.C: Import is not defined as deleting all existing Case Types.
optionExplanations.D: Import is not restricted to the BA who authored the proposal.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team choosing an industry template in Blueprint asks what value the template provides beyond a blank starting point. What is the correct answer?

options.text: Templates instantly apply decades of Pega's accumulated best-practice expertise to the proposed application design
Templates provide random sample data records for populating the demo environment with realistic test data
Templates provide server provisioning scripts pre-configured for the chosen industry's compliance requirements
Templates contain only Access Role definitions specific to the chosen industry, with no Case Type or workflow content

practiceQuiz.hint: What does 'best-practice template' mean in the context of Blueprint's value proposition?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint templates embody Pega's accumulated best-practice expertise for the industry — they accelerate design by embedding proven patterns. Templates are starting points; all elements are editable after generation.

optionExplanations.A: The template supplies a reusable industry design starting point.
optionExplanations.B: Test records are not the primary design value asked here.
optionExplanations.C: The template does not provision compliant production servers.
optionExplanations.D: Its scope includes workflows and data, not only security roles.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Lead System Architect (LSA) wants to use Blueprint to accelerate the start of a new project. Place the four Blueprint workflow steps in the correct order: (1) Refine the AI proposal, (2) Describe the app in business terms, (3) Export/import into Pega Platform, (4) Receive AI-generated Case Types, Data Models, Personas.

options.text: Describe in business terms → Receive AI proposal → Refine the proposal → Export/import into Pega Platform
Export/import into Pega Platform → Describe in business terms → Receive AI proposal → Refine the proposal
Receive AI proposal → Describe in business terms → Refine the proposal → Export/import into Pega Platform
Describe in business terms → Export/import into Pega Platform → Receive AI proposal → Refine the proposal

practiceQuiz.hint: Think: describe first, get the proposal, refine it, then bring it into Pega.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Describe the goal, receive a proposed design, refine it with stakeholders, then export the technical file and import it. The importing developer follows the project’s authorized workflow.

optionExplanations.A: Describe the need, review the proposal, refine it, then import.
optionExplanations.B: Importing before a design exists reverses the workflow.
optionExplanations.C: The business description precedes the proposal it informs.
optionExplanations.D: Refinement should precede import in this design sequence.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team is using Pega Blueprint to accelerate the design of a new Customer Service application. Which TWO statements correctly describe the Pega Blueprint workflow?

options.text: The Describe phase uses AI to generate a structured application Blueprint from a natural language business description
The Refine phase allows the SA to review and adjust the AI-generated Blueprint before importing it into Pega Platform
The Import phase requires the SA to manually recreate all Rules in Dev Studio based on the generated Blueprint PDF
The Describe phase permanently locks the Blueprint, preventing any refinements before import

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint's three phases are Describe (AI generates), Refine (SA adjusts), Import (Pega creates Rules).
practiceQuiz.rationale: In Pega Blueprint, the Describe phase takes a natural language business description and uses AI to generate a structured application outline. The Refine phase lets the SA review and modify the generated Blueprint before committing to it. The Import phase then automatically generates the Pega Rules — the SA does not need to manually recreate them in Dev Studio.

optionExplanations.A: The initial description guides AI-assisted design generation.
optionExplanations.B: Refinement supports reviewing the proposed model before implementation.
optionExplanations.C: Import does not require manually recreating every rule from a PDF.
optionExplanations.D: The proposal remains editable rather than permanently locked.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is explaining when to use Pega Blueprint versus App Studio to a business stakeholder. Which TWO statements correctly differentiate the two tools?

options.text: Pega Blueprint uses AI to accelerate the initial application design phase, generating a Case Type outline from a business description
App Studio is used to configure and refine the actual Pega Rules and Case Type logic after the Blueprint has been imported
Pega Blueprint replaces App Studio entirely once a Blueprint is generated, eliminating the need for any further Rule configuration
App Studio must be used first to generate the initial Blueprint before Pega Blueprint can be launched

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint accelerates the design start; App Studio is where the actual rule configuration happens afterward.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pega Blueprint accelerates the initial design phase using AI to create a structured outline from business requirements. After the Blueprint is imported into Pega Platform, App Studio is used to configure, refine, and extend the generated Rules. Blueprint supplements App Studio rather than replacing it, and Blueprint is the starting point — not App Studio.

optionExplanations.A: Blueprint accelerates the initial collaborative design proposal.
optionExplanations.B: App Studio configures the application after importing the proposal.
optionExplanations.C: The imported starting point does not eliminate further configuration.
optionExplanations.D: Blueprint generation does not require beginning inside App Studio.

quickRecap.value: Separate SaaS workflow design at pega.com/blueprint; Platform development access is not a prerequisite. Follow SaaS access requirements.
Augments App Studio and other tools — does not replace them; applies decades of best practices via templates.
From a business-terms description: Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas — then refined collaboratively.
Import the technical .blueprint file, not the PDF. Review build/inherit/reuse/skip choices, classes and permissions; configure and test afterward.
In the documented new-app workflow, created assets except Access Roles go into a Branch. Outside the branch does not mean not created.
NOT required to import a Blueprint.
Start from industry best-practice templates (e.g., Customer Service for Insurance) and refine for the organization.
